'''Iwatsuta Shrine''' (石津太神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Nishi-ku|en|Nishi-ku|qid=Q296095|lt=Nishi-ku, Sakai}}, {{ill|Sakai|en|Sakai|qid=Q193428|lt=Sakai}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|qid=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917284|qq= 近代社格制度}}, it is one of the candidate locations for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha}} "Iwatsuta Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳}} alongside {{ill|Ishizu Shrine|ja|石津神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ishizu Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11586788}} in {{ill|Sakai-ku, Sakai|en|Sakai-ku, Sakai|qid=Q1042008|lt=Sakai-ku, Sakai}}. Both claim to be the "oldest Ebisu shrine in Japan."

== Enshrined Deities ==
The principal deities enshrined are {{ill|Hiruko|ja|蛭子命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiruko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q1067028|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1067028}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|八重事代主命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}}, and {{ill|Ame no Hohi|ja|天穂日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Hohi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノホヒ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10940685}} (ancestral deity of the Ishizutsure clan). {{ill|Amaterasu|abstract|Q455602|ar|أماتيراسو|ary|أماطيراسو|az|Amaterasu|bcl|Amaterasu|be|Аматэрасу|be_x_old|Аматэрасу|bew|Amatérasu|bg|Аматерасу|ca|Amaterasu|cs|Amaterasu|da|Amaterasu|de|Amaterasu|el|Αματεράσου|eo|Amaterasu|es|Amaterasu|et|Amaterasu|eu|Amaterasu|fa|آماتراسو|fi|Amaterasu|fr|Amaterasu|gl|Amaterasu|he|אמטראסו|hi|अमातेरसु|hr|Amaterasu|hu|Amateraszu Ómikami|hy|Ամատերասու Օմիկամի|id|Amaterasu|it|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|jv|Amaterasu|ka|ამატერასუ|ko|아마테라스 오미카미|la|Amaterasu|lb|Amaterasu|lt|Amaterasu|lv|Amaterasu|min|Amaterasu|ml|അമതേരസു|mni|ꯑꯃꯇꯦꯔꯁꯨ ꯑꯣꯃꯤꯀꯃꯤ|ms|Amaterasu|nl|Amaterasu|nn|Amaterasu|no|Amaterasu|or|ଆମାତେରାଶୁ|pa|ਆਮਾਤੇਰਸ|pl|Amaterasu|pt|Amaterasu|ro|Amaterasu|ru|Аматэрасу|sco|Amaterasu|sh|Amaterasu|simple|Amaterasu Ōmikami|sk|Amaterasu Ómikami|sl|Amaterasu|sr|Аматерасу|su|Amaterasu|sv|Amaterasu|ta|அமதெரசு|th|อามาเตราซุ|tl|Amaterasu|tok|jan sewi suli Amatelasu|tr|Amaterasu|uk|Аматерасу|uz|Amaterasu|vi|Amaterasu|wuu|天照大神|zh|天照大神|zh_min_nan|Amaterasu|zh_yue|天照大神|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}} (from Tsunagami Shrine) is also worshiped, along with {{ill|Takeminakata|ja|建御名方富命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeminakata|qid=Q9150391}} through shrine amalgamation.

== History ==
According to legend, this area was once a seaside location where {{ill|Izanagi|en|Izanagi|qid=Q813858|lt=Izanagi}} and {{ill|Izanami|en|Izanami|qid=Q682306|lt=Izanami}} set {{ill|Hiruko|ja|蛭子命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiruko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q1067028|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1067028}} adrift, eventually reaching this site. It is said that Hiruko placed five sacred stones ("Goshiki-no-Ishi") here, naming the place "Ishizu." The location where these stones were interred is marked near the intersection before the shrine's torii gate.

The shrine was built on August 10 in the 7th year of Emperor {{ill|Emperor Kōshō|en|Emperor Kōshō|qid=Q312841|lt=Kōshō}}, per imperial command. Over the years, it received patronage from the Imperial Court, including visits by emperors. Although the shrine possessed extensive lands, it suffered destruction during the {{ill|Genna|en|Genna|qid=Q635245|lt=Genna era}} and later conflicts. During the construction of {{ill|Osaka Castle|ja|大阪城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osaka Castle|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大坂城|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q321242}}, {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|en|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|qid=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Hideyoshi}} revered the shrine as a guardian deity. {{ill|Kimura Shigenari|en|Kimura Shigenari|qid=Q840196|lt=Kimura Shigenari}} contributed gold to reconstruct the shrine. In the {{ill|Meiwa|en|Meiwa|qid=Q1146161|lt=Meiwa era}}, it resolved a dispute over {{ill|Ofuda|en|Ofuda|qid=Q2500908|lt=ofuda}} distribution with {{ill|Nishinomiya Shrine|en|Nishinomiya Shrine|qid=Q705297|lt=Nishinomiya Shrine}}, gaining a broader following.

== Shrine Buildings ==
The main shrine consists of two halls: the northern hall, housing Hiruko, Kotoshironushi, and Ame-no-Hohi, is built in {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|en|Nagare-zukuri|qid=Q210684|lt=Nagare-zukuri}} style, while the southern hall, dedicated to Takeminakata and Amaterasu, is in {{ill|Kasuga-zukuri|en|Kasuga-zukuri|qid=Q3193781|lt=Kasuga-zukuri}} style. Both halls are connected by a shared gabled worship hall constructed during the {{ill|Hōreki|en|Hōreki|qid=Q1194397|lt=Hōreki era}}.

The grounds include a large stone where Hiruko is said to have rested and several auxiliary shrines such as {{ill|Iwatsuta Inari Shrine|ja|磐山稲荷社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwatsuta Inari Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135579301}}, Hachiman Shrine, and White Snake Shrine.

== Festivals ==
The shrine is known for its fire festival, the "Yassai Hossai," held on {{ill|December 14|en|December 14|qid=Q2382|lt=December 14}}. Participants write wishes on paper attached to 108 sacred wooden bundles, which are burned to divine fortunes based on the falling direction of the flames. Men carrying an effigy of {{ill|Ebisu|ja|戎神}} perform fire-walking while chanting "Yassai Hossai." This ritual is believed to offer protection from pain and misfortune.<ref>Goto, Michi. "Japanese Strange Festivals," Seikyusha, 1996. ISBN 4787231308.</ref>
